# Known-center Phase I for the bounded-witness discovery SDP

This closes a complexity-interface correction to `EFFECTIVE_PORT.md`.
The bounded-witness premise supplies existence of a strict certificate,
but does NOT supply that feasible center. Therefore the known-center
Turing theorem is NOT invoked directly on the original discovery SDP.
The following ordinary Phase I construction acquires its actual premise.

Controlling primary: de Klerk–Vallentin1507.03549v2, Theorem1.1 (attributed
there to Grötschel–Lovász–Schrijver). Its input includes a KNOWN rational
feasible matrix X0 and known inner/outer Frobenius radii in the equality
affine space. It returns a rational feasible point at any positive
requested objective accuracy in polynomial time in the SDP size, data
bits and logarithmic radius/accuracy parameters. Here every such input
is constructed for a Phase I problem, not assumed for the discovery set.

## 1. Known equality point

Use the degree/boxes of `EFFECTIVE_PORT.md`: k=(D-3)/2, d=k+2,
N=ell-d, n_G=6*binom(ell+3,3), A=A_P, Gamma=3B64^ell.
Let x list all homogeneous P coefficients, nu and upper-triangular Q
entries. The exact coefficient equations have rational form Ex=f.
The desired inequalities are

    Q-(m/8)D_ell >=0,
    b_i+x_i>=0, b_i-x_i>=0 for every coordinate i,

where b_i is2A for primitive coefficients,2Gamma for Gram entries,
and Lambda+2 for nu. These coordinate boxes also bound all possible
unknown normalizers; nothing is supplied by an optimizer.

There is an explicit rational equality point x0: set P=0 and nu=0, then
represent the known polynomial

    T^(N+k+1) D_0 F

by a symmetric Gram Q0 in the full basis A^alpha h_j, |alpha|=ell.
Every monomial of A-degree2ell and h-degree2 splits into two such basis
monomials. Assign its coefficient to a diagonal Gram entry, or equally to
the two symmetric off-diagonal entries. This is the same elementary exact
coefficient operation used in the original certificate qualifier. Q0 may
be indefinite; it is NOT mislabelled a feasible point. Acquisition is
finite rational monomial arithmetic, polynomial in the finite map/output
size. No alpha, min-eigenvalue, gap or convex feasibility oracle is needed.

# Root receiving of the bounded-witness search operation

30 October 2026. **ACCEPTED at its explicit bounded-witness mathematical
and weak-optimization scope.** This is a substantive analytical reconstruction,
not a model/optimizer run or a practical degree claim. Constructive overlap
is disclosed: root authored HIERARCHY.md and HEAT_BRIDGE.md; A independently
developed the quantitative kernel/Phase-I port reviewed here.

Whole-read bindings:
EFFECTIVE_PORT.md SHA3dbd0cb92298b6688783b11259ec32fb903e511a3c922f3a04d505c533e37033,
PHASE_I.md SHAa1af7cc7c3de1f7add2fc5181733dca1a0fbab99edae378684968053570a1ce9.

I reconstructed the S3 beta-kernel normalization and second moment, rotational
derivative/C1 estimates, rational odd homogenization and paid nu/coefficient
rounding. Their total margin loss is strictly below the stated allowance.
The coefficient boxes pay homogenization and numerical magnitude, rather
than claiming access to the unknown alpha.

For the matrix stage, I reconstructed the normalized (x.y)^(2ell) moments,
the harmonic eigenvalue product and inverse-error sum at ALL degrees. The
S3 degree2j projection norm is bounded by sqrt((2j+1)^2)=2j+1; the explicit
ell makes the shifted inverse-kernel density uniformly positive. Its exact
spherical-moment Gram has rational entries and is PSD by its defining
integral. Adding (m/4)D_ell gives a paid weighted PD margin and directly
recovers mT|h|²/4, without a multinomial conditioning loss. The entry/bit
bounds are conservative and valid at the stated fixed variable dimension.

One load-bearing interface gap was raised and corrected: existence of an
unknown alpha does NOT supply deKlerk--Vallentin's known feasible center.
The final PHASE_I constructs an exact indefinite equality Gram at P=nu=0,
then a common artificial slack and scalar boxes. Its displayed X0>=2I is
a KNOWN rational strictly feasible matrix for that different SDP. Relative
Frobenius radius1/2, outer radius, objective and map injectivity are explicit.
The promised witness gives t<=-s; objective accuracy s/2 therefore acquires
an actual t<0 certificate. A nonnegative near-optimal output excludes the
DECLARED bounded witness class only. It does not refute QC or unbounded
heat-form witnesses, nor decide bounded-class membership on success.

The paid eta,W,Lambda bounds are essential. Numerical values lead to very
large polynomial degrees/SDPs;
